p95.method: Nearest-rank ceil(n*95/100), applied independently to actual completed marker elapsed_us samples

operations: read uploaded JSON, nft rules and command/process logs
compare actual marker/receipt fields and hash file bytes
independently decode classic pcap frames with PowerShell
independently recompute nearest-rank p95 from uploaded samples

interpretation: Production SDK relay DROP run 41607840510 completed/failure at this exact source. Its twenty-trial runtime step succeeds and the original runtime receipt has passed=true. The only failed job step is subsequent strict cargo clippy: chain.rs:173:21 uses expect_err and violates clippy::expect_used, exit 101. Runtime success and enclosing job failure are both retained. No original failure is rewritten.

The official ZIP and all 141 extracted files are independently hashed. All 139 producer payload entries and 75 command-log entries match actual bytes, with overlapping sets not additional distinct files. Both process log SHA256 fields also match. strict-clippy.log was generated after the producer files manifest, has no producer digest entry, and is verified by official ZIP identity and actual downloaded bytes. The complete official raw job log is independently hashed.

All twenty uploaded ready and completed markers, combined slice entries and final SDK samples match by trial index and value. Each trial has a distinct original exporter digest and transport-group observation, path_epoch=2, 98,335 verified FileRead bytes and true original/spare UDP release and joined-file-worker markers. The exact runtime test source checks retained original inner binding and original deadlines, fixed business generation, real socket rebinds, file source verification and finished worker status before publishing completion. These are original runtime assertions/receipts; absent source-file payload bytes and executable bytes are not claimed as independent local file or binary verification.

Independent nearest-rank p95 recomputation from the twenty completed-marker elapsed_us samples yields 2,631,009 microseconds, rank 19 of 20. Maximum is 2,694,883 microseconds; the unchanged threshold is 3,000,000 microseconds. Marker, combined slice and final SDK duration samples are equal. Original monotonic timing values are retained runtime receipts; local recomputation verifies aggregation without claiming to remeasure the private runner clock.

Each downloaded nft rules file and counter JSON matches only the original active relay sport/dport and permits the distinct standby. All twenty per-trial install/counter/delete commands succeed, both rule counters match slice records, and total actual packet hits are 407. An independent PowerShell classic-pcap decoder validates all 11,424 complete Ethernet/IPv4/UDP loopback records, IP/UDP lengths and no fragmentation; original/standby QUIC Initial and standby UDP-after-DROP counts match every producer trial count. These are captured records, not unique packets or additional business cases. Encrypted business payload is not independently decrypted.

The runtime process log identifies the dedicated namespace and all four nonzero ordinary UID fields. Both original SDK and capture processes finish with expected return codes and no forced cleanup; uploaded process-log digests match. Owned nft cleanup succeeds, the original PID listing is empty before deletion, namespace deletion succeeds and the namespace is absent afterward. tcpdump reports the same captured record count and zero kernel drops. Per-trial physical and worker markers remain distinct from namespace/process cleanup observations.

Exact source/workflow/run and before/after Cargo.lock claims match the exact Git blobs. Clean private runner state and executable SHA256 remain producer provenance where those private bytes are absent. The producer scope is controlled loopback relay DROP with production SDK automatic polling and approved file-only business, without a manual migration request. production_migration_protocol_exercised=true is retained for that runtime scope; w14_complete=false, ac22_passed=false and interactive_recovery_qualified=false remain unchanged. Public NAT, independent relay-process crash, Windows native input/media, interactive p95, adaptive PMTU, full cancellation/poller matrix, whole acceptance and release eligibility are not claimed.

No product source, assertion, stack, timeout, selector, public HTTPS trust, ingress/late/PTS/capture or Luanti threshold is changed by this audit. The local independent decoder reads already uploaded packet bytes only; it does not invoke project parsers, compilers, formatters, clippy, tests or target programs.
